results.content: Shifting trade policies and fluctuating tariffs triggered volatility in the early months of President Trump’s second term, though markets have since recovered. In 2025, the S&P 500 generated a total return of 17.9%. Year-to-date through August 7, 2026, the S&P 500 is up 14.1%. During the primary years of former President Biden’s four-year term (2021-2024), the S&P 500 generated a 66.3% total return. Trump’s first term (2017-2020) saw an 81.3% total return. Europe's headline index tracks 600 large, medium, and small capitalization companies across 17 European countries, and is essentially the continent's equivalent of the S&P 500. The Stoxx 600 is up 10% in 2026 so far, slightly behind its North American counterpart, which has returned 13.5% over the same period.
